item.content:encoded:
Hamid died before talking to Derringer, so the Hamid that talked to Derringer is either a ghost of some sort, or not the real Hamid. This is what Derringer means by "voodoo bullshit [coming] back to haunt us."

The latter point is more or less left to the "there is no canon" rule; this was mostly meant as a look into a timeline where the Chicago Spirit is consumed by Fifthism in an attempt to gain profit gone wrong.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm a big fan of this whole concept — however, I noticed there is some chronological inconsistencies in Derringer's letter.

Sufi Abdul Hamid, Queenie's ex-husband, came to me today, said the fifthists were up to something.

[…]

But I'm starting to notice some consequences, Chappell. And I don't want to sit idly by while some voodoo bullshit comes back to haunt us. Hamid died in a plane crash last week.

Additionally, (assuming that this article is based on our baseline timeline), I think Chappell could not receive this letter; while Hamid died in 1938, Chappell was detained by the Foundation in 1933.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I would never have thought that the interactions between the Spirit and Fifthism would have this much interesting potential. It's a real treat to see a group that really is totally unprepared to deal with Fifthists have to deal with Fifthists. They don't even have terminology to describe memetics and cognitohazards, only the edits included after the fact start to conceptualize Fifthist influence as a "disease of the mind." Really swell stuff.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Wow, this really went beyond what I expected. The use of the edits after the fact, hints at the bizarre fifthist cognitohazards, just really well done. Can't wait to see what you come up with next! +1
